# Kathinakkhandhaka (Kd 7)

**ID:** Kd 7
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Kathinakkhandhaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kathinakkhandhaka* is the seventh chapter of the Mahāvagga within the Khandhaka section of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [von Hinüber 1996; Norman 1983]. Often translated as "The chapter on the robe-making ceremony" or "On kathina" [Norman 1983], it sets forth the legal procedures and monastic regulations governing the *kaṭhina* cloth-offering and robe-making ceremony, which takes place during the last month of the rainy season after the completion of the *vassa* residence. Performance of the ceremony extends monks' robe privileges until the end of the cold season, and the majority of the text provides an intricate, technical legal analysis of the conditions that either terminate or maintain those privileges [von Hinüber 1996; Norman 1983].

  Machine alignments via DharmaNexus link the chapter to Tibetan Vinaya treatises (such as the *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga*, *Vinayasūtravyākhyāna*, and *Vinayavastu*) and Sanskrit Vinaya remains [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies 2,304 matching passages across 85 texts, showing extensive text reuse with the Parivāra (*Kathinabheda*, Pvr 16), adjacent Khandhaka sections (especially the *Cīvarakkhandhaka*, Kd 8), the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4 and AN 5), and the primary Vinaya commentaries and subcommentaries (*Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā*, *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā*, and *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā*) [DharmaNexus].

 In modern Southeast Asian history, modernist Cambodian reform monks including Chuon Nath and Huot Tath produced an abbreviated Khmer translation of the *Kathinakkhandhaka* under the auspices of the Buddhist Institute to standardize monastic conduct [Hansen 2007].
